That makes the recipe auditable without minting new entries. Rewriting either fingerprint to match a recomputation would ORPHAN the existing entry and must not be done. Human fix only — no pipeline stage may repair this automatically.

watchNotes.title: `clean:local` runs `rm -rf ~/.foundry/anvil/tmp/*`, reaching outside the repository into shared per-user state
watchNotes.detail: `clean:local` ends with `rm -rf ~/.foundry/anvil/tmp/*` — a destructive delete against a directory the project does not own, executed twice per `npm run dev` (once in job 1, once inside `deploy:local`). THE OBSERVED-CONSEQUENCE HALF IS SOLIDLY NEGATIVE AND IS NOT DISPUTED: ~/.foundry/anvil/tmp/ was sampled every 0.5s for 30s spanning BOTH clean:local runs and was EMPTY at all 60 samples; anvil in this invocation (no --state, no --fork-url) never writes there; the chain survived, all 381 broadcast transactions landed, and it was still mining at block 799 (evidence/anvil-tmp-watch.log). BUT THE FORKED-ANVIL BRANCH WAS NEVER TESTED: whether a CONCURRENTLY-RUNNING forked anvil belonging to another task — which DOES keep state under that path — would have its state files removed was not exercised in any sample. PARKED RATHER THAN FILED because no consequence was observed and none is claimed; filing on an untested branch would be overstatement, and deleting it from view would be a Law-1 recall failure. Parking is the correct third option and this note IS the visible channel.
watchNotes.toResolve: Cheap and decisive, one command: start a second `anvil --fork-url $RPC_MAINNET --state <dir>` alongside, run `clean:local`, and observe whether the forked instance's state files are removed. That settles it either way.
watchNotes.recommendationIfConfirmed: Scope the cleanup to the repository: drop `rm -rf ~/.foundry/anvil/tmp/*` from `clean:local` entirely, or replace it with a targeted removal of this project's own anvil state path. A project script should never rm -rf a shared user directory it does not own.
